dedupe_keys.name: nyc 911 end to end response time data

description: The NYC 911 End-to-End Data set breaks New York City emergency response time into its segments for each first-responding agency: the police (NYPD), the fire department (FDNY) and emergency medical services. For each week, agency and final incident type it gives the number of incidents and average and median seconds from call to first pickup, calltaker handoff, fire and EMS pickup, job creation, dispatch, travel and arrival, including first arrival at multi-agency incidents. The producer is the Mayor's Office of Operations of the City of New York, published on NYC Open Data. Coverage is citywide and weekly, from November 2013 to August 2026 as read today, updated monthly. Data are downloadable as CSV or JSON and queryable through the Socrata API without registration, under the NYC Open Data terms of use; no licence is named in the metadata. Caveats: values are weekly aggregates, not individual calls; there is no location breakdown; incident type definitions changed over time and are documented on a separate page. Simulation uses: calibration and validation of call-handling, dispatch and travel-time distributions in emergency medical and fire service simulation models, and benchmarking of response performance during disruptions such as storms or pandemic surges. Related records: the San Francisco fire and EMS calls for service (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) give call-level times for another city.
